findings.what: The picture runs the 900 kVA start, so before Check the Recovers to tile reads 79.5% while the question says 85%, and a right answer of 72.3% then reveals Torque 63.3%; give this screen no picture (nofig) or ask about the 79.5% it shows.

findings.where: Screen 6 text and the run's stall state (motor red, say line 'It has stalled')
findings.what: Every start that recovers below 90% is drawn and told as a certain stall (750 kVA recovers to 89.7% and stalls while 700 kVA at 93.8% gets away; screen 6 ends 'The motor stalls.'), but the 90% rule only promises enough torque for most loads and the explain says 'may stall', so say 'With this load, the motor stalls' and 'so with this load it cannot make enough torque'.

findings.where: Screen 8, Torque tile and the end-of-run say line
findings.what: The Torque tile reads 100% for the soft starter (and star-delta) right under 'Both give the motor less torque as it starts', because it compares each start with itself on full voltage, which no screen says; label it 'Torque vs full voltage, %' or hide it for the reduced starters, and change the say line's 'made 100% of its torque' to match.

The recovered voltage appears in a new form, 2.5 ÷ (1 + 1.5 × 900 ÷ 630), with no word that it is screen 2's divider with E = 2.5 in place of 1 and 1.5 in place of 0.15, and 'it reaches only' has no clear subject; write 'The same divider now gives 2.5 × 0.70 ÷ (0.70 + 1.5) = 79.5%' and trim elsewhere to stay under 90 words (87 now).

'The motor's starting impedance is 630 ÷ 600 = 1.05 per unit' skips why a load's per-unit impedance is the set's kVA over the load's kVA (a load drawing the set's full kVA at full voltage is 1 per unit, a bigger load a smaller impedance), and the hints on screens 5, 9 and 11 all lean on that step; add one sentence and trim to stay under 90 words (86 now).

A 'roughly' question is graded at three points only (600, 700, 800 A, each ±0.5), so 650 or 750 A, inside the hint's own '6 to 8 times', is marked wrong and the hint then repeats the range he answered within; grade 700 A with a tolerance of 100 A.

The brief promised power management, blackout and restoration in outline (blackout prevention, heavy consumer blocking, blackout recovery, dead-bus synchronising, loads back in steps), the set as a whole (the engine's energy split, kW from the engine and kVA from the alternator, no long running under about 30% load) and closing screens mixed from the whole course, but only motor starting and one line on power management are taught and no later course takes this ground; add one SHOW screen on blackout prevention and recovery and one mixed puzzle from lessons 5 or 7, or list the cut in the brief's left-out list for Dan.
The feeder label shows the 600 kVA motor while the question is about a 900 kVA start; open the screen at 900 kVA.

The answer, 93.3%, is the figure screen 8 just gave for the same 300 kVA on one set, and the feeder label already shows '300 kVA', the hint's step, so it can be answered by recall; screen 10 then gives 93.3% a third time unexplained, so pick another size or say once that the same 300 kVA per set gives the same 93.3%.
600 kVA at 0.4 giving 240 kW was told on screen 4 and in every run's say line, so this is recall; use another size such as 900 kVA (360 kW) and rework the slips.

'Starting loads one at a time helps the same way. In one worked case it cut the starting kW needed by 40%.' narrates a source's example, and 'the same way' is wrong because sequencing keeps each step small rather than cutting the reactance; say 'Starting loads one at a time keeps each step small. Three motors started one after another, not together, can need 40% less starting kW.'
'You are about to press Start.' points at a Start button this screen does not show before the answer, and the read-through has none; say 'The motor is about to start.'
